author: WP18
summary: Updated-for-d6e9ff05 chapter separating build, host-start, structural and pixel evidence for the five browser renderers: HTML_DOM's automated Chromium suite, SVG_DOM's manual harness, and WebGL/Canvas without browser execution. Current at TARGET, with small corrections (six HTML_DOM pages, WEBGL1 in no workflow). Tutorial 105 already carried the status table; the evidence ladder, harness mechanics and common verification shape are now on the web deep dive.

sections.heading: Web III: Five Renderers, Four Kinds of Evidence
HTML_DOM: automated browser and pixel evidence
SVG_DOM: browser harness plus bundle CI
WEBGL2 and WEBGL1: translation without browser execution
CANVAS: startup failure before renderer evidence

concepts.section: Web III: Five Renderers, Four Kinds of Evidence
concepts.text: The five browser identities are not five equally verified implementations; build, host-start, structural and pixel evidence are separate kinds.

The ladder: build (compiled and linked), host start (a JavaScript host ran startup), structure (a real browser observed renderer-specific DOM/SVG invariants), pixels (the compositor produced expected colours at sampled points).
Higher rungs do not erase lower ones: a pixel sample can miss a malformed object tree and a structural assertion can miss blending, so the strongest suite does both.

concepts.section: HTML_DOM: automated browser and pixel evidence
concepts.text: HTML_DOM has the only automated browser run: htmldom-ci pins emsdk 6.0.3, installs Playwright Chromium, starts Xvfb and runs run-htmldom-test-suite.sh, which serves six pages (smoke, pixel, stress, dispose, host-integration, memory) and waits for a window verdict flag.
concepts.note: Six pages confirmed; the workflow header still says four. Sharp-runtime pin caveat applies.

concepts.section: HTML_DOM: automated browser and pixel evidence
concepts.text: The HTML_DOM driver samples the real compositor: a Playwright screenshot is decoded inside the page into a canvas and read with getImageData at decisive points, because the renderer-owned DOM alone would not prove what Chromium composed.
tokens: not what the renderer's DOM claims

concepts.section: HTML_DOM: automated browser and pixel evidence
concepts.text: The host-integration page rewrites the HTML response with page.route() (addInitScript runs too late) to prove CNA refuses to seize a host-owned DOM element and creates no viewport; the timing mechanism is part of the proof.

concepts.section: SVG_DOM: browser harness plus bundle CI
concepts.text: SVG_DOM's browser driver checks an SVG-namespace root and flush-slot children, a hidden SDL canvas and four composited scissor-order points; the namespace checks are anti-spoofing evidence another renderer cannot fake with a similar picture.

concepts.section: SVG_DOM: browser harness plus bundle CI
concepts.text: The SVG_DOM runner has no workflow or CTest caller; the multi-renderer web job builds WEBGL2, CANVAS, HTML_DOM and SVG_DOM into one bundle, checks archive symbols and registry entries, and launches no browser.

target.evidence: .github/workflows/emscripten-multi-renderer-ci.yml (llvm-nm, registry count); no caller of scripts/run-svgdom-browser-test.sh

concepts.section: WEBGL2 and WEBGL1: translation without browser execution
concepts.text: WEBGL2 and WEBGL1 have no browser execution in the tree; a bare-Node attempt only shows the wrong host, and no WEBGL1-generated GLSL has been compiled by a real WebGL 1 implementation.

target.evidence: no WebGL browser harness under scripts/ or registration at TARGET

concepts.section: WEBGL2 and WEBGL1: translation without browser execution
concepts.text: Context creation, shader-version compatibility, uploads, presentation and context loss stay open for WebGL; context-loss code exists but no test loses and restores a context and demands a fresh visible frame.

target.evidence: modules/renderers/easygl (context-loss handling); no such test registered

concepts.section: CANVAS: startup failure before renderer evidence
concepts.text: CANVAS builds (it is in the multi-renderer bundle) but has no browser run; its manual checklist is the only browser route, so the next useful test is an HTTP-served page with a verdict and a compositor sample, not another Node run.

The status matrix per identity: HTML_DOM automatic browser, structure and pixels; SVG_DOM manual runner with structure and four samples; WEBGL2 and CANVAS bundle-linked only; WEBGL1 admitted by CMake but built by no workflow.
concepts.note: Corrected: WEBGL1 is not in the bundle workflow.

concepts.text: The matrix is deliberately asymmetric: a build entry says nothing about frame one and a few sampled pixels say nothing about full rendering parity.

A common harness shape: loopback HTTP, a named window verdict with timeout, failure on console errors and page exceptions, a renderer-specific structural token, a few composited pixel samples, and archived logs and screenshots.
tokens: fail on console errors and page exceptions

concepts.text: The central rule is to prove the intended runtime engaged: identity, execution and visible output are three separate facts and the evidence should contain all three.
tokens: Identity, execution and visible output are three separate facts

issues.text: Only HTML_DOM has an automatic browser run; SVG_DOM's browser runner has no workflow or CTest caller, CANVAS/WEBGL1/WEBGL2 have no browser harness, and WEBGL1 is built by no workflow.
htmldom-ci.yml's header comment says the suite drives four pages; run-htmldom-test-suite.sh runs six (stale comment).
